sentence: This project sets up a course about cancer research for people with several characteristics that affect their risk and recovery from cancer.
This project provides genomic and epigenomic services, such as DNA sequencing and DNA methylation analysis, to cancer researchers.
This project tests whether turning tumor-promoting macrophages into tumor-suppressive macrophages helps immune checkpoint blockade work against glioblastoma.
This project combines insertable and wearable devices with computational methods to measure metabolites and estimate macronutrient intake.
This project combines mass spectrometry imaging with ultrafast online microdroplet digestion to identify more proteins directly in tissues.
This project tests whether the innate immune response helps detect poor quality oocytes and removes the affected follicles.
This project uses zebrafish to look for diagnostics, therapies and therapeutic targets for bleeding and clotting disorders.
This project studies how cells sense nucleotides and respond to nucleotide depletion, to target cancer cells while sparing normal and immune cells.
This project studies the plasticity of skeletal stem cells in craniofacial bone formation and craniofacial bone diseases.
This project studies T cells and surrounding cells in the bone marrow to find out why immunity is impaired in acute myeloid leukemia.
This project studies a fusion transcript of two genes found in lung adenocarcinoma and whether its protein makes the cancer more aggressive.
This project builds a web-based computational toolkit that evaluates the toxicity of medical devices for sensitization, irritation and cytotoxicity.
This project builds statistical machine learning methods that help diagnose rare diseases in a timely way.
This project studies how romantic partners affect each other's suicide risk in young adults, including those with borderline personality disorder.
This project develops methods to study the structure of large biological macromolecules that interact through electrostatic interactions.
This project builds an AI-powered resource that helps scientists choose or develop non-animal models of biological systems and diseases.
This project tries to find out what makes rhabdomyosarcoma cells spread to other parts of the body in children.
This project looks for approaches and agents to combat diseases of the nervous system, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and nervous tissue injury.
This project studies how a specific receptor helps abnormal cells grow in myelodysplastic syndrome and develops therapies to suppress that growth.
This project builds more accurate genotyping methods to tell whether malaria returns after treatment because the drug failed or because of a subsequent infection.
